selfCarePage.heading: Self-Care and Support
selfCarePage.concern: This work takes a personal toll.
selfCarePage.intro: Working with youth at risk for suicide is some of the hardest clinical work there is. These tools help you spot burnout early, build resilience into your practice, provide tips and tricks from your peers, and let you schedule a consultation call with our licensed clinical psychologist.

why.heading: Why This Matters
why.intro: Building resilience into your practice isn't a luxury — it's part of doing this work well and staying in it for the long haul.

cards.lead: This work is hard — and that's not a reflection of your skill.
cards.body: Vicarious trauma and compassion fatigue are a normal response to sustained high-acuity work, not a sign you're doing something wrong.
Every therapist on the Rise roster carries a caseload like yours — peer support and consultation exist because this work is genuinely heavier when carried solo.

cards.lead: Therapist burnout is real, and support helps.
cards.body: Therapists doing this work report high exhaustion and emotional demand, and need more support

testimonials.text: Burnout is challenging. It's very hard seeing people in really difficult places over and over, especially when your entire caseload looks like that.
Having someone else to call when a case gets heavy makes all the difference. I don't have to carry it by myself anymore.
I started blocking ten minutes before my hardest sessions just to breathe. It sounds small, but it changed how I show up.

mindfulness.heading: Session Mindfulness
mindfulness.intro: A brief grounding practice before a hard session, and a brief reset after one.

pre.title: Pre-Session Mindfulness
pre.subtitle: Before you begin
pre.intro: Take a minute to ground yourself before you walk in.
prompts: Notice three things you can see in the room around you.
Unclench your jaw and drop your shoulders.
Name one thing you want to hold onto from this session.

post.title: Post-Session Mindfulness
post.subtitle: After you finish
post.intro: Take a minute to reset before you move to the next thing.
prompts: Name one thing from that session you'll let go of before the next one.
Notice how your body feels right now, without judging it.
Note anything you want to remember to follow up on later.

peerTherapists.heading: Peer Therapist One-on-One Support
peerTherapists.intro: Connect directly with another Rise therapist for informal, one-on-one peer support — not a substitute for supervision, just someone who gets it.
